report.narrative: GMV in the week of 2017-08-07 was R$145,391, up 6.1% from the prior 4-week average of R$136,993, but the change is not statistically anomalous (robust z-score 0.06). Decomposition shows the increase was driven by a 10.9% rise in AOV (contributing +R$14,591) offset by a 4.3% drop in orders (contributing -R$6,193). Segment scans across customer_state, product_category, seller_state, payment_type and repeat-customer flag found no segment whose share shift was both historically unusual (|hist_z| ≥ 4) and statistically significant (BH q ≤ 0.05). The largest share movers — customer_state SC, MG, ES, PR and product_category cool_stuff, watches_gifts, auto — all failed significance tests (q-values 0.16–0.65). Therefore, no significant root cause is identified for this week's GMV change.
recommended_actions: Monitor GMV weekly; the current change is within normal variation.
Track AOV and order volume separately to catch diverging trends early.

Therefore, no significant root cause is identified for this week's GMV increase.
recommended_actions: Monitor GMV in subsequent weeks to see if the upward trend persists.
No immediate action required; the change falls within normal weekly variation.

report.narrative: GMV rose 38.8% (R$ 88,508) in the week of 2018-07-30 versus the prior 4-week average, but the headline change was not statistically anomalous (z=1.57). The only segment with a statistically significant and historically unusual shift was Santa Catarina (SC), whose share of GMV dropped from 3.25% to 0.50% (p=2.0e-11, hist_z=-4.28), dragging GMV down by R$ 6,975. The overall increase was driven by broad-based growth across large states — São Paulo (+R$ 61,562), Minas Gerais (+R$ 11,555) and Rio de Janeiro (+R$ 9,258) — but none of those share changes reached the significance threshold (|hist_z|<4.0). The SC decline appears to be a data or fulfilment issue rather than a demand shift.
recommended_actions: Investigate order processing and seller coverage in Santa Catarina for the week of 2018-07-30 to confirm whether the drop is a data gap or a real fulfilment problem.
Monitor SC GMV in the following weeks; if it rebounds, treat the week as a one-off data issue.

report.narrative: GMV rose 38.7% to R$316,603 in the week of 2018-07-30 versus the prior 4-week average of R$228,298, driven by a 44.6% jump in orders (1,980 vs 1,369) while AOV fell 4.1% to R$159.90. recommended_actions: Monitor next week to see if the order surge persists or reverts.
Track marketing spend and promotional calendar for the week to explain the broad order increase.

This decline was more than offset by broad-based growth across other categories (notably housewares +82.1329%, telephony +151.86%, bed_bath_table +62.2324%) and a surge in São Paulo state (+62.7887%), which together drove the net increase.
recommended_actions: Investigate why health_beauty GMV collapsed (stock-outs, listing issues, or a promotion that ended) and restore assortment/availability.
Replicate the successful drivers in housewares, telephony and bed_bath_table (promotions, marketing, seller onboarding) to sustain growth.

report.narrative: GMV rose 31.7058% (R$ 72383.7) in the week of 2018-07-30 versus the prior 4-week average, but the headline change was not statistically anomalous (z=1.2768). A scan of all segments revealed one significant root cause: the housewares category's share of GMV dropped from 7.1325% to 1.8828% (p=2.326e-17, q=2.326e-17), dragging GMV down by R$ 10449.55 (-14.4363% of the total change). This mix effect was the only segment whose shift was both historically unusual (hist_z=-5.2413) and statistically significant after multiple-test correction. The overall GMV increase was driven by broad-based growth across many categories (e.g., health_beauty +41.4691%, telephony +151.86%) and a surge in São Paulo orders (+66.6333%), but none of those individual share shifts reached significance.
recommended_actions: Investigate why housewares GMV share collapsed: check stock-outs, seller deactivations, or promotional calendar gaps in that category.
Monitor whether the broad-based growth in other categories (health_beauty, telephony, bed_bath_table) is sustainable or driven by one-off events.

report.narrative: AOV fell 3.6% to R$160.98 in the week of 2018-04-23 versus the prior 4-week average of R$167.00 (e1). The decline was driven almost entirely by the watches_gifts category, whose average order value dropped from R$238.23 to R$149.96 — a rate effect that explains 93.5% of the total AOV change (e6). This rate change is highly significant (p=4.7e-11, q=4.7e-11) and historically unusual (hist_z=-5.40) (e3). The category's share of orders nearly doubled (5.5% to 9.9%), but the share shift was not statistically significant (q=5.4e-11, hist_z=3.93 < 4.0 threshold) (e5). The price drop in watches_gifts reduced weekly GMV by an estimated R$9,378 (e4). No other segment showed a significant rate or mix effect.
recommended_actions: Investigate pricing, promotions, or product mix changes in the watches_gifts category during the week of 2018-04-23.
Monitor watches_gifts AOV in subsequent weeks to confirm whether the drop persists or reverts.

report.narrative: The on-time delivery rate in the week of 2017-05-29 was 97.25%, a 0.36% increase versus the prior 4-week average of 96.90%. This change is not statistically anomalous (robust z = -0.10). Segment scans found no segment whose rate or share change was both historically unusual (|hist_z| ≥ 4) and statistically significant after multiple-test correction (BH q ≤ 0.05). The largest rate drops were in Espírito Santo (87.5% vs 97.4%) and Bahia (90.3% vs 98.0%), and the largest rate improvement was in bed_bath_table (100% vs 95.0%), but none met the significance threshold. Therefore, no significant root cause is identified for this week.
recommended_actions: Continue monitoring on-time delivery weekly; the current fluctuation is within normal variation.
Investigate Espírito Santo and Bahia logistics if their lower on-time rates persist in subsequent weeks.

report.narrative: The on-time delivery rate fell slightly from 97.1% to 96.9% in the week of 2017-08-14 (a -0.19% change vs the prior 4-week average). The headline change was not anomalous, but a scan of segments revealed that sellers in Rio de Janeiro (RJ) saw their on-time rate drop sharply from 98.6% to 79.2% (a -19.4 pp decline on 24 orders). This RJ seller-state rate effect was statistically significant (p=0.00023, q=0.00023) and accounted for 259% of the total change, meaning it more than offset improvements elsewhere (e.g., SP sellers improved). The impact was roughly 4.7 fewer on-time orders from RJ sellers that week.
recommended_actions: Investigate logistics or carrier issues specific to RJ sellers during that week (e.g., local strikes, weather, warehouse delays).
Monitor RJ seller on-time performance weekly and set up an alert if the rate falls below 90%.

report.narrative: The on-time delivery rate for the week of 2017-08-14 was 97.12%, virtually unchanged from the prior 4-week average of 97.10% (change +0.019%). This RS rate decline contributed -5,458% of the total change (i.e., it pulled the overall rate down by ~1.03 percentage points), but was offset by improvements in other states such as SP and RJ. Approximately 10 fewer orders were delivered on time in RS than expected.
recommended_actions: Investigate logistics or carrier issues specific to Rio Grande do Sul during that week (e.g., weather, strikes, hub delays).
Monitor RS on-time rate weekly and set an alert if it falls below 90% to catch recurrences early.

report.narrative: On-time delivery rate collapsed from 93.7% to 54.8% in the week of 2018-04-23 (a 41.5 pp drop, z = -8.44). The decline was broad-based and statistically significant across every major segment tested. The single largest driver was São Paulo state (customer_state=SP), where the on-time rate fell from 97.6% to 40.5%, accounting for ~64% of the total change. Sellers in São Paulo (seller_state=SP) saw an even steeper drop to 39.3%, and new customers (is_repeat_customer=0) fell to 54.7%. High-volume categories such as furniture_decor (44.4%), auto (48.6%), and telephony (35.3%), plus the dominant boleto payment method (51.7%), all experienced rate declines of 40-60 pp. The pattern points to a systemic logistics or carrier failure centred on São Paulo rather than a mix shift.
recommended_actions: Engage the primary carrier(s) serving São Paulo immediately to diagnose the root cause of the delivery failure.
Prioritise proactive customer communication and compensation for orders in SP, furniture_decor, auto, and telephony categories paid via boleto.
Add real-time carrier SLA monitoring dashboards for SP and the top affected categories to catch recurrences early.

report.narrative: The on-time delivery rate dropped 1.41 percentage points (from 97.1% to 95.7%) in the week of 2017-08-14, a statistically anomalous decline (z = -6.43) [e1]. The sole significant root cause is sellers in Santa Catarina (SC), whose on-time rate collapsed from 98.9% to 61.7% (p < 0.001, q = 1.97e-15) [e3]. This segment alone accounts for 126.7% of the total decline, meaning other states partially offset the drop [e5]. The impact equals roughly 17.5 fewer on-time orders that week from SC sellers [e4]. No other segment (MG, RS, watches_gifts, new customers) reached significance after multiple-test correction [e6, e7, e8, e9].
recommended_actions: Investigate logistics carriers and fulfillment centers serving Santa Catarina for capacity or routing issues that week.
Set up an automated alert when any state's on-time rate falls more than 5 pp below its 4-week average.

report.narrative: Cancellation rate spiked from 0.21% to 15.99% in the week of 2018-04-23 (a 7,596% increase, z-score 53.2). Credit-card orders saw the highest segment rate at 20.26% (up from 0.18%), while São Paulo sellers and customers, plus the sports_leisure, watches_gifts and bed_bath_table categories, all showed statistically significant rate increases. The pattern points to a systemic issue affecting new buyers across payment, geography and product lines rather than a single segment.
recommended_actions: Investigate whether a platform-wide change (e.g., checkout flow, fraud rules, payment gateway) was deployed that week and disproportionately impacted first-time buyers.
Check credit-card authorization/decline logs for the week to see if a spike in failed payments triggered automatic cancellations.
Review seller onboarding or policy changes in São Paulo that could have caused mass order rejections.

This sharp drop was driven by a rate effect (behaviour inside the segment changed), not a mix effect. No other segment passed the significance threshold (BH q ≤ 0.05 and |hist_z| ≥ 4.0).
recommended_actions: Investigate the 'cool_stuff' category for product quality, shipping, or seller issues that could explain the sudden drop in review scores.
Monitor 'cool_stuff' review scores weekly to see if the low scores persist or revert.

report.narrative: AOV fell 13.27% to R$145.71 in the week of 2018-07-30 versus the prior 4-week average of R$168.0 (e1). The only statistically significant driver was a mix shift: fashion_bags_accessories jumped from 1.15% to 18.39% of orders (share test p=2.101e-182, e3), while its internal AOV and item prices did not change significantly (rate tests p=0.4431 and p=0.6164, e6, e7). This mix shift alone explains 75.18% of the AOV drop and equates to an estimated R$-38563.98 GMV impact (e4). The category's share of items also surged (1.04% to 17.48%, p=7.578e-197, e8), confirming a broad order-mix change rather than a price change.
recommended_actions: Investigate why fashion_bags_accessories orders surged (promotion, new seller, catalog change) and whether the low-AOV mix is sustainable.
Monitor category-level AOV weekly to catch mix shifts early; consider AOV targets by category to avoid aggregate surprises.

report.narrative: AOV dropped 16.9% (R$ -25.31) in the week of 2017-08-14 versus the prior 4-week average, a statistically anomalous decline (z = -6.04). The largest driver was a mix shift: fashion_bags_accessories surged from 2.0% to 28.1% of orders, contributing 78.6% of the AOV drop (R$ -27570.2 impact). Simultaneously, the AOV within major segments fell sharply: São Paulo sellers (rate effect, R$ -29713.2), new customers (rate effect, R$ -32340.07), and credit-card orders (rate effect, R$ -22122.22). Paraná customers' share halved, partially offsetting the decline (R$ +1144.02). The value-per-item component accounted for 91.6% of the total AOV change.
recommended_actions: Investigate the fashion_bags_accessories surge: check for a promotion, new seller onboarding, or catalog change that inflated low-AOV orders.
Review pricing and discounting for São Paulo sellers and new-customer cohorts; the broad-based rate decline suggests a platform-wide price or mix shift.
Monitor Paraná customer acquisition; its shrinking share removed a higher-AOV segment.

report.narrative: AOV dropped 11.0% (R$18.37) in the week of 2018-04-23 versus the prior 4-week average, a statistically anomalous decline (z = -3.54). The largest single driver was a mix shift: electronics orders surged from 2.8% to 19.6% of all orders, and because electronics carry a lower AOV (R$70.10 vs R$71.90 baseline), this alone pulled overall AOV down by R$16.30 (88.7% of the total change, R$32,657.91 GMV impact). Simultaneously, new-customer orders (97.4% of volume) saw their AOV fall R$17.88 (R$35,840.18 impact), and both credit-card (R$15.79 drop, R$24,479.32 impact) and boleto (R$30.17 drop, R$10,399.11 impact) payment types experienced significant rate declines. The decomposition shows value-per-item drove 83% of the AOV drop, consistent with the electronics mix shift and lower per-item prices across payment types.
recommended_actions: Investigate why electronics order share jumped 7x in one week — check for a promotion, new seller onboarding, or catalog change.
Diagnose the new-customer AOV decline: compare acquisition channels, first-order discounts, and product mix vs. repeat buyers.
Review credit-card and boleto pricing/promotions that week; the broad-based rate drop suggests a platform-wide price change or coupon.

report.narrative: The average review score dropped sharply from 4.03 to 3.24 stars in the week of 2017-05-08, a 19.5% decline that is highly anomalous (z = -10.3). Boleto and customer-state SP also showed significant rate drops. All five segments passed significance tests with extremely low q-values, confirming a broad-based deterioration in customer satisfaction rather than a mix shift.
recommended_actions: Investigate operational issues affecting SP-based sellers in early May 2017 (e.g., delivery delays, product quality, or seller onboarding changes).
Review the new-customer experience (onboarding, first-order communication, packaging) to understand why first-time buyers rated significantly lower.
Check whether a payment-gateway or fraud-rule change for credit-card orders coincided with the drop.

report.narrative: The average review score dropped sharply from 4.11 to 3.27 stars in the week of 2018-04-23, a 20.3% decline that is statistically anomalous (z = -5.39). report.narrative: The average review score dropped sharply from 4.23 to 3.29 stars in the week of 2017-08-14, a 22.2% decline that is a clear anomaly (z = -21.1). The decline is driven by a broad-based deterioration in ratings across almost every segment, but the strongest statistical signals come from sellers in São Paulo (SP), where the average score fell from 4.21 to 2.96 stars (p = 4.194e-60), and from first-time buyers (is_repeat_customer = 0), whose scores fell from 4.24 to 3.29 stars (p = 2.226e-49). Credit-card orders, customers in SP and RJ, and the categories garden_tools, bed_bath_table and housewares all show significant rate drops (p < 1e-5). Because the effect is pervasive, it likely reflects a systemic issue such as a delivery delay or platform-wide service disruption that week rather than a single segment problem.
recommended_actions: Investigate logistics and delivery performance for the week of 2017-08-14, especially for sellers in São Paulo, to identify any widespread shipping delays.
Review customer-support tickets and seller communications from that week for clues to a platform-wide issue (e.g., payment gateway outage, policy change).
Monitor review scores in the following weeks to confirm whether the drop was a one-off event or the start of a sustained trend.

recommended_actions: Monitor AOV weekly; the current dip is within normal variation.
Track health_beauty item prices separately—they showed a significant price drop that did not translate into a detectable AOV impact this week.

recommended_actions: Monitor AOV for the next 1-2 weeks to see if the elevation persists before launching any targeted campaigns.
Set up automated weekly AOV alerts with a lower threshold (e.g., |z| ≥ 3) to catch sustained shifts earlier.
